notes: Annual report of the Board of Park Commissioners for the year ending June 30, 1892. Curated: Stow Lake's first section, the Children's Quarters and its merry-go-round cover, the beach building.

coverage.remaining: Not placed: the Aviary (300 by 150 feet; no page), the steel and iron footbridge from the Music Grounds to Chicken Point, a rose garden near the Park Lodge (not today's), Sweeney's Observatory.

findings.description: The grading of the first section of the lake, east of Strawberry Hill, let by contract at 8½ cents a cubic yard, was finished in February 1892; its bed and banks were sealed with ten inches of tamped clay under three inches of rolled rock, and the water held. The second section, north of the hill, was graded, and the whole ring around the hill was under contract.

findings.description: Having bought out the private interests in the merry-go-round, the donkey rides and the restaurant at the Children's Quarters, the Park Commissioners put a permanent cover of antique design over the merry-go-round, built under the supervision of the architect A. Page Brown.

findings.description: At the Children's Quarters the ball grounds were being turned into a lawn for boys under fourteen, walks were laid out, the donkey run changed, and an asphalt rink built for roller skating and bicycles.

findings.description: For visitors to the beach the Park Commissioners put up a two-story building for about $8,000, with a ladies' sitting room, a general sitting room and a large balcony looking out on the ocean upstairs, a long room for bicycles below, and sheds for horses and carriages.
